articles.topic: Modern HRT doesn't increase heart disease risk
articles.headline: Modern Hormone Therapy Safe for Heart Health, Large Study Shows
articles.body: A major study of over 52,000 women ages 45-59 found that contemporary hormone replacement therapy did not increase the risk of heart attacks, strokes, blood clots, or early death. The findings came from long-term health records in Israel and were presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026. The results challenge old concerns about HRT and suggest that modern formulations in oral, patch, and gel forms appear safe for women starting treatment around menopause without prior heart disease or clotting history.
articles.takeaway: If you're considering HRT around menopause, modern formulations appear safe for your heart—discuss timing and dosage with your doctor.

articles.topic: Ketogenic diet reduces liver fat fast
articles.headline: Keto Diet Cuts Liver Fat by Two-Thirds in Just Four Months
articles.body: A new clinical trial found that the ketogenic diet dramatically reduced liver fat and improved metabolic health compared to Mediterranean and low-fat diet approaches, even when participants lost similar amounts of total weight. After four to five months, keto dieters saw significantly greater reductions in the harmful fat that accumulates in the liver. This matters because excess liver fat is linked to metabolic dysfunction and cardiovascular issues. The study shows that diet composition, not just calories, shapes how your body stores fat.
articles.takeaway: If you have signs of metabolic dysfunction, keto's effect on liver fat reduction might be worth exploring—but discuss with your doctor first.

articles.topic: Ice bath timing affects performance recovery
articles.headline: When to Use Ice Baths: Timing Matters More Than You Think
articles.body: A comprehensive review of 161 studies found that cold-water immersion is powerful for recovery—but timing is everything. Ice baths reduce post-exercise soreness and speed recovery, making them useful for sore muscles the day after hard training. However, explosive performance drops in the hours immediately after an ice bath due to muscle cooling. The key insight: cold-water immersion won't harm your aerobic fitness or endurance adaptations if used strategically. It's not a one-size-fits-all tool, so match the protocol to your training goals.
articles.takeaway: Use ice baths after hard sessions when recovery matters more than the next workout—avoid them if you're training explosiveness the same day.

articles.topic: Aerobic exercise reshapes heart and blood vessels
articles.headline: How Aerobic Exercise Rebuilds Your Cardiovascular System at the Cellular Level
articles.body: New research published in the American Journal of Physiology examined how aerobic exercise transforms the heart and surrounding tissues. The study found that exercise modulates the fatty tissues around blood vessels and the heart itself, activating cellular pathways that extend far beyond just building aerobic capacity. These fat-tissue changes represent an underappreciated mechanism for how exercise protects cardiac health. The takeaway: regular aerobic work doesn't just make your heart pump harder—it fundamentally restructures the tissues that support cardiovascular function, offering protection against obesity-related heart disease.
articles.takeaway: Consistent aerobic exercise reshapes your cardiovascular system at the cellular level—the benefits run deeper than your fitness tracker can measure.

workout.title: Easy Movement & Core Awareness: Gentle Activation Flow
workout.tip: Focus on movement quality, not reps or speed. Each exercise should feel smooth and controlled. If your breathing becomes labored, you've gone too hard for a recovery day—dial back intensity immediately.
workout.warmup: 3 min: 20 sec jumping jacks (or step-touch if needed), 10 arm circles, 10 leg swings (forward-back each leg), 5 inchworms, 10 glute bridges

exercises.name: Scapular Push-Up (Isometric Hold Emphasis)
exercises.notes: High plank position, hands under shoulders. Lower body 2 inches by retracting shoulder blades (no elbow bend), then push back to start. This teaches scapular stability without heavy load—foundational for push patterns.

exercises.name: Dead Hang Shoulder Activation
exercises.notes: Hang from bar (or assisted band if needed). Let shoulders relax into full stretch, then gently shrug shoulders up and down 5–10 times. Teaches lat and shoulder stability passively.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat Hold (Unloaded)
exercises.notes: Hold hands at chest in goblet position (no weight), squat to comfortable depth. Pause at bottom for 2 breaths, focusing on knee tracking and upright torso. Restores squat pattern without loading.

exercises.name: Bird Dog Series (Slow & Deliberate)
exercises.notes: On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg. Pause 2 breaths at full extension, feel core brace. Return slowly. This builds anti-rotation stability and core awareness safely.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with 2-Sec Hold
exercises.notes: Lying on back, knees bent, feet flat. Drive through heels, squeeze glutes at top, hold 2 seconds. Focus on hip extension, not lumbar arch. Reactivates posterior chain after running or sitting.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Flow (Spinal Mobility)
exercises.notes: Hands and knees position. Cow: drop belly, lift gaze, open chest. Cat: round spine, tuck chin. Move with breath, no rush. Mobilizes entire spine and promotes parasympathetic activation.

workout.cooldown: 3 min: child's pose 20 sec, supine figure-4 stretch 20 sec each side, lying hamstring stretch 20 sec each side, final 30 seconds supine with arms overhead, slow breathing
workout.description: A 30-minute low-stress bodyweight movement session combining light calisthenics, breathing drills, and form refinement for active recovery. This session reintroduces movement patterns (push, pull, squat, hinge) at minimal intensity, promoting blood flow and proprioceptive awareness after intense training without accumulating fatigue. Ideal for beginners building movement literacy while recovering from strength or fat-loss blocks.

meal.title: Beef Jerky & Sharp Cheddar Snack Pack
meal.description: Portable, shelf-stable protein and fat combo designed to fuel strength athletes between workouts or as a quick desk snack. The combination of beef jerky's concentrated protein and aged cheddar's calcium supports muscle maintenance and bone density.
meal.instructions:
1. Open jerky package.
2. Portion cheddar into a small container or wrap in parchment.
3. Pack together for a grab-and-go snack.
meal.tip: Buy jerky in bulk from Costco or online to cut costs. Choose low-sugar varieties (under 4g per serving) to avoid unnecessary carbs between meals.
